_comment: Allowance, in differing pixels at RGB565, for web/page_vs_golden.js.
The page entry in web/anim_bench.html is the approved design and the
firmware is meant to draw it. Zero is the rule and 40 of the 44
animations meet it, so a new port is expected to.
Every number below is debt recorded against bead gm-pciz, measured on the
worst of golden frames 30, 120 and 210. Lower one when you fix it.
Never raise one to make a check pass. A raise needs a reason in 'notes'
saying why the measurement changed meaning, and the mean deviation per
channel has to have fallen: more pixels differing by less is progress,
and the pixel count alone cannot see that.

ripples: Raised from 14672 to 18369 on 2026-09-12, by e3a74acd, and this is an
improvement rather than a regression. The page used to draw its random
numbers from mulberry32 while the firmware used xorshift32, so the two
sides rained in different places entirely. The old count was low only
because the pond was empty at two of the three golden times and there
was almost nothing to disagree about. Both sides now share the stream
and agree on every drop. What is left is the firmware's integer
distance tracker, whose one pixel phase error is documented in the
file header, spread over far more ring pixels than before.
The mean absolute deviation per channel is the number that shows it:
5.02, 3.49 and 3.31 at the three frames before, 2.82, 2.79 and 2.76
after. Fixing the tracker is what takes this to zero.
Confirmed by measurement on 2026-09-13 and accepted as debt. A variant
that takes the page's per-pixel arithmetic (exact float centre, real
square root, the page's envelope and cosine, and the page's double row
swell) is exact: 0 differing pixels at all three frames. The distance
and the two per-pixel tables are 97% of the gap and the row swell 3%.
It is not shipped because the page's model is per-pixel libm over about
100,000 ring pixels a frame: the host bench band goes from 0.118 to
0.541 ms a frame, and it would have to be transcribed bit for bit into
two hand-written Xtensa kernels that have no fallback flag. The reason
and the numbers are in AnimRipples.cpp's header.
